newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, Phillips in $750mln petrochemical deal.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, Phillips in $750mln petrochemical deal.

text.p: Qatar on Sunday signed an agreement in principle with Phillips Petroleum Co to set up a $750 million petrochemical complex, Qatar's Oil Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah said.
The state's Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) will hold 51 percent in the joint venture. Phillips will have 49 percent.

Designed to produce 500,000 tonnes a year of ethylene and 467,000 tonnes a year of polyethylene, including high-density polyethylene (HDPE) and linear low-density polyethylene, it will go on stream in 2000, Attiyah said.
It will also include a Hexene-1 plant with an annual capacity of 50,000, said the minister, who signed the deal with Phillips chairman and chief executive officer Wayne Allen.
Attiyah said the complex will use Phillips' proprietary polyethylene and Hexene-1 manufacturing and catalyst technologies.

Polyethylene will be sold in Asian, African, European and Middle East markets. "Hexene-1 will be used as feedstock in the polyethylene facilities and excess output will be sold to the world market," Attiyah said.

J. Robert Benz, vice-president of Phillips' global ventures and international relations, told Reuters he hoped the project's design would be completed by the end of 1997. He said construction would start next year.
The new complex is the oil and gas-rich state's third petrochemical complex to cash in on its massive gas reserves -- the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's.
The first, Qatar Petrochemical Co, is already producing. The second, Qatar Vinyl Co is under construction.
There was no word on how the project would be financed. But a senior QGPC official told Reuters: "The same pattern will be followed as in the case of other Qatari projects".
Other projects have been 70 percent financed by international loans and export credits and 30 percent by equity.
